land.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis, taken by Shebitku about 712

successors.note: Infobox "Succeeded by: Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt". Necho I of Sais, who later ruled under Assyrian protection, is called a local Saite king under Taharqa on the 24th page; the Saite line returns as the Twenty-sixth Dynasty after a gap of about fifty years.

capitals.name: Sais (Sa el-Hagar)
capitals.note: Infobox: Sais; the page calls the dynasty "a short-lived group of pharaohs who had their capital at Sais in the western Nile Delta."

rulers.name: Tefnakht
rulers.note: Infobox 732-725 (the table says 3 years, the dates span seven).

rulers.name: Bakenranef (Wahkare)
rulers.note: The 24th page gives 725-720 and a deposition in 720; the 25th Dynasty and Piye pages put Shebitku's capture of Sais about 712, followed here.

correction.text: Sais and the western Delta, with Memphis: the page says Bakenranef's authority was recognised in much of the Delta including Memphis

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Twenty-fourth Dynasty. The page names Sais as capital and Memphis (Serapeum stelae of Bakenranef's years 5 and 6) but gives no frontier and no area. Piye took Memphis in his campaign of about 728 but did not hold it; Tefnakht's coalition "formed an alliance of the Delta kinglets", so the wider Delta is drawn as the dynasty's tint after 728 (ledger vassal events), not as its land.

ledger.note: 732: Tefnakht of Sais founds the Twenty-fourth Dynasty. The infobox gives Tefnakht 732–725 and the page dates his conquests to 732; the Third Intermediate Period page has Sais c. 732–720. He "formed an alliance of the Delta kinglets" and tried to conquer Upper Egypt (Piye page: he besieged Herakleopolis).

728: Piye's army meets Tefnakht's coalition. Tefnakht besieged Herakleopolis and drew Nimlot of Hermopolis to his side; Piye won "complete victory at Herakleopolis", took Hermopolis and Memphis (Piye page; the Victory Stele page says year 20 of his reign).

region.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis

ledger.note: 728: Tefnakht submits to Piye. The Victory Stele page has "Tefnakhte submits to Piye"; the Piye page says he conceded defeat by letter but "refused to personally pay homage to the Kushite ruler". He keeps Sais and the western Delta as a tributary king.
728: Piye returns to Nubia, "never to return to Egypt", leaving the Delta kings in place; the campaign ends.

region.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis

ledger.note: 712: Shebitku ends the tributary status of Sais by conquering it.

region.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis

ledger.note: 712: Shebitku takes Sais and the Delta. The 25th Dynasty page says he conquered the whole Nile Valley "around 712 BC"; the 24th page says Shebitqo attacked Sais, captured Bakenranef and burned him alive, but dates the deposition to 720. The Piye page puts the defeat in Shebitku's second regnal year.

region.text: Sais, the western Delta and Memphis

ledger.note: 712: the dynasty ends with the death of Bakenranef. Two of the pages opened (25th Dynasty, Piye) point to about 712; the 24th page's own date is 720, which is the alternative.

wars.name: Piye's invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: Piye defeated the coalition at Herakleopolis, took Hermopolis and Memphis and received the Delta kings' submission before returning to Nubia.
wars.note: Tefnakht's siege of Herakleopolis opened the war; no year is given for it. The dating of Piye's year 20 is 725-732 depending on page.

wars.name: Shebitku's conquest of the Delta
wars.outcome: Shebitku took Sais, captured Bakenranef and had him burned alive; the dynasty ended.
wars.note: Year: "around 712 BC" (25th page), his second regnal year (Piye page); the 24th page dates the deposition to 720.

certainty.note: No frontier is given by any page; the core is Sais and Memphis.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for this dynasty; me-03-b's Twenty-second Dynasty dossier already names it as counterpart (loss of Sais at 732) and the Kush dossier calls it 'Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt (Sais)'. Only two of the five pages open the question of its end: the 24th page says Bakenranef was deposed in 720, the 25th Dynasty page and the Piye page say Shebitku's conquest of the Delta was around 712 (second regnal year). 712 is used for the end here and for the matching gain in twenty-fifth-dynasty-of-egypt; if a later reviewer prefers 720, change both dossiers. The page gives no area, no frontier and no founding date for the dynasty itself (732 is Tefnakht's accession). Necho I (a Saite king killed in 663) is not a separate state: he reigns under Assyrian protection from 671 and the pages open do not make him a dynasty; the Saite line is the Twenty-sixth, written by me-03-c.
